handbookNote: Source: official Colorado Driver Handbook (form DR 2337, 12/05/24 revision), published by the Colorado Division of Motor Vehicles (Colorado Department of Revenue) and downloaded directly from dmv.colorado.gov/sites/dmv/files/documents/DR_2337_Jan2025.pdf, linked from the DMV's own Driver Education page (dmv.colorado.gov/drivereducation). Full text extracted with pdftotext and saved to temp/handbooks/co/driver.txt. Every question in this bank is grounded in specific statements from that handbook text (traffic laws, GDL/minor-driver rules, DUI/DWAI Table 1 penalties, seat belt and child-restraint tiers, signs/signals/markings, right-of-way, speed limits, freeway/passing rules, Colorado-specific mountain/winter/rural driving content, railroad and RTD light rail rules, distracted/aggressive driving, and crash/emergency procedures) -- no invented facts and no generic 'common knowledge' padding. Exam mechanics: confirmed the Colorado knowledge/permit test ('Driving Knowledge Test', also called the Class D Knowledge Test) is TIMED at 60 minutes, confirmed via both dmv.colorado.gov/home-driving-knowledge-tests (official DMV FAQ: 'Test takers will have 60 minutes to complete the test') and the DMV's official @Home testing vendor FAQ at coathometesting.com/faq ('There is a 60-minute time limit to complete the test'). Despite thorough research of the DMV site, its Driver Education and @Home Testing pages, and the official testing vendor's FAQ, Colorado does NOT appear to publicly publish a specific fixed item (question) count or a numeric passing-score percentage for this exam anywhere in official sources -- unlike many other states, this is genuinely not disclosed, so that figure is intentionally left UNCONFIRMED rather than guessed or reused from another state. The handbook itself confirms the test covers handbook content: road signs, DUI, driving rules, safety rules and legal items, offered in English and Spanish, with a $6.50 test fee (first and subsequent online attempts) plus an $11.50 state DMV fee. Content depth: the 27-page handbook body (after front matter) supports substantial genuine depth in DUI/DWAI law (Table 1's BAC/points/fine/jail/public-service matrix), traffic signs/markings/lane controls (incl. roundabouts and Diverging Diamond Interchanges), right-of-way, minor-driver/GDL rules, and notably rich Colorado-specific mountain, winter (snow/ice), and rural driving content -- this pool of 320 raw questions across 20 topic buckets is honestly supported by that material, not padded; a small number of ambiguous/garbled PDF-table fragments (e.g. a scrambled two-column 'Points to remember' truck/bus sidebar) were deliberately excluded rather than guessed at.
